decisions.reason: The cross-Requirement effect is already fully represented by the existing message-171 MODIFY, including the left-arm cap-height relationship, right-arm hierarchy, overall scale constraint, and removal of the obsolete height_relative_to_e_and_l key.
Scaling the E and L cap height is owned by the dedicated cap-height Requirement and does not change their architectural construction, originality, or design-language rules.
The cap-height change does not alter the existing bottom-baseline alignment rule; the message's acceptance of the common baseline is already represented separately as runtime verification.
The source changes E/L height relative to the second V and does not modify the approved Hero V geometry.
The source message's Variation B and tighter-kerning selection is already fully represented by the existing message-171 MODIFY; the cap-height change adds no further kerning-state change.
The client asks to scale the E and L around the existing second V rather than modify or redraw the second V glyph geometry.
Reaffirming that the accent must be a copy of the Hero V right arm does not necessarily change its positional peak-alignment rule.
The copy/paste instruction reiterates the candidate's existing exact one-to-one derivation requirement and establishes no new value.
The source does not change the terminal's shape, conviction, or shared treatment; it only uses the second V arms as height references.
The source concerns monochrome wordmark geometry and does not affect the deferred champagne material treatment.
The cap-height decision does not change the obligation to provide design rationale with review rounds.
